key_insight: Combining NLP from clinical notes with structured EHR data found social and behavioral risk factors across all 17 domains and linked several of them to frequent ED use in cardiovascular patients.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help healthcare teams better identify patients with cardiovascular disease who have unmet social or behavioral needs and are at higher risk of repeated emergency department visits.
method: Built a custom NLP system to extract 17 SBDH domains from unstructured clinical notes.
Combined note-derived findings with ICD-10 Z codes and screening questionnaire data from the EHR.
Used multivariable logistic regression to test associations with high ED utilization (≥5 visits) after adjustment for demographics and chronic conditions.
evidence_signal: In 4,844 adults with cardiovascular disease, 526 (10.9%) were frequent ED users, and note-based NLP increased SBDH detection compared with codes and questionnaires alone.
watch_item: The study is observational and shows association, not causation; performance may depend on note quality, local documentation practices, and EHR integration.
paper_title: Integrating structured and unstructured EHR data to characterize social and behavioral factors associated with frequent emergency department use among patients with cardiovascular disease
